title: Psychic Tomb to Triadic Womb: Toward a Developmental Ecology of Relational Sacred Mindfulness
abstract: This article presents the Triadic Good-Enough Womb, an integrative developmental ecology within Relational Sacred Mindfulness (RSM), a Winnicottian-informed humanistic and transpersonal psychotherapy for reactivating interrupted maturational processes and receiving dissociated somatosensory affect. Using hermeneutic phenomenology, I trace an evolving Quinean epistemological web shaped by monastic training, spiritual direction, dissertation research, a 10-year follow-up inquiry, published clinical theorizing, disconfirming phenomena, postdoctoral coursework, archetypal guidance, and reflexive therapist-researcher participation. The phenomenon that most disrupted my earlier web occurred when a client experienced Jesus holding her infant self and then dropping her, revealing that the appearance of a loving sacred presence did not necessarily constitute a developmentally facilitating relationship. In dialogue with Gadamer, Winnicott, Jung, Kalsched, Kohut, Benjamin, Woodman, Tillich, May, and others, the intervention expanded from facilitating a sacred relationship that receives dissociated affect to tending a developmental ecology. Relational somatic mindfulness forms the first layer of the Triadic Good-Enough Womb, therapeutic attunement, empathy and mirroring the second, and RSM the third. Together, somatic holding, assessment of projection, and attachment to a transpersonal presence capable of receiving dissociated affect may create conditions in which a psychic tomb becomes less necessary and protected life resumes movement toward maturation.
